parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving fire, injury, property damage, emergency evacuation, or emergency intervention within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a preliminary incident report. Other confirmed thermal incidents shall be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers of a serious incident involving their model within 72 hours of confirming the incident, and provide material safety updates as they become available.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving fire, injury, property damage, emergency evacuation, or emergency intervention within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a preliminary incident report. Other confirmed thermal incidents shall be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers of a serious incident involving their model within 72 hours of confirming the incident, and provide material safety updates as they become available.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving fire, injury, property damage, emergency evacuation, or emergency intervention within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a preliminary incident report. Other confirmed thermal incidents shall be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers of a serious incident involving their model within 72 hours of confirming the incident, and provide material safety updates as they become available. Reports shall include the model, incident date and location, known consequences, and immediate safety measures; a complete investigation report is due within 30 days. Manufacturers shall maintain incident records and correct any omissions promptly.

parameters.quote: A failure rate above 5% requires prompt notification to the regulator, a regulator-approved corrective-action plan, and retesting within a regulator-set timeframe. Exceeding 5% shall not by itself require an automatic sales ban; the regulator may impose proportionate interim safeguards or restrict sales where necessary to address a demonstrated safety risk. Manufacturers shall provide per-model methods, sample sizes, and results to the relevant regulator and directly to current and prospective customers for that model. Individual-company per-model failure rates shall not be published to the general public; industry reporting may use aggregated, non-identifying results.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: A failure rate above 5% requires prompt notification to the regulator, a regulator-approved corrective-action plan, and retesting within a regulator-set timeframe. Exceeding 5% shall not by itself require an automatic sales ban; the regulator may impose proportionate interim safeguards or restrict sales where necessary to address a demonstrated safety risk. Manufacturers shall provide per-model methods, sample sizes, and results to the relevant regulator and directly to current and prospective customers for that model. Individual-company per-model failure rates shall not be published to the general public; industry reporting may use aggregated, non-identifying results.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo standardized sustained-heat testing at 55 °C using a documented, reproducible method and a representative sample. A failure rate above 5% requires prompt notification to the regulator, a regulator-approved corrective-action plan, and retesting within a regulator-set timeframe. Exceeding 5% shall not by itself require an automatic sales ban; the regulator may impose proportionate interim safeguards or restrict sales where necessary to address a demonstrated safety risk. Manufacturers shall provide per-model methods, sample sizes, and results to the relevant regulator and directly to current and prospective customers for that model. Individual-company per-model failure rates shall not be published to the general public; industry reporting may use aggregated, non-identifying results.

parameters.quote: New models shall include a remote emergency shut-off capability. For units already installed when this standard is adopted, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or other approved means of remote emergency shut-off within six years of adoption. Where a unit cannot reasonably be retrofitted, the manufacturer shall notify its owner and provide an equivalent safety measure approved by the regulator.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New models shall include a remote emergency shut-off capability. For units already installed when this standard is adopted, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or other approved means of remote emergency shut-off within six years of adoption. Where a unit cannot reasonably be retrofitted, the manufacturer shall notify its owner and provide an equivalent safety measure approved by the regulator.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New models shall include a remote emergency shut-off capability. For units already installed when this standard is adopted, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or other approved means of remote emergency shut-off within six years of adoption. Where a unit cannot reasonably be retrofitted, the manufacturer shall notify its owner and provide an equivalent safety measure approved by the regulator. Shut-off systems shall be secure, available to authorized emergency responders or operators as appropriate, and shall not prevent safe local operation.

parameters.quote: New units shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard. The suppression system shall be evaluated for effectiveness and shall not create an additional hazard under foreseeable installation and operating conditions. Manufacturers shall provide customers with instructions for inspection, maintenance, and safe response to an incident.

parameters.quote: If a model exceeds 8 confirmed thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and submit the incident data and a proposed corrective-action plan for review. The regulator shall assess incident severity, evidence of a common cause, exposure, and the effectiveness and timeliness of proposed measures, and may require a recall where necessary to address an unacceptable risk.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: If a model exceeds 8 confirmed thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and submit the incident data and a proposed corrective-action plan for review. The regulator shall assess incident severity, evidence of a common cause, exposure, and the effectiveness and timeliness of proposed measures, and may require a recall where necessary to address an unacceptable risk.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before purchase, customers shall receive model-specific sustained-heat test results, known material thermal hazards, safe installation and operating instructions, and clear steps for reporting an incident. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of any new material safety risk and provide required precautions and repair or replacement information. If a model exceeds 8 confirmed thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and submit the incident data and a proposed corrective-action plan for review. The regulator shall assess incident severity, evidence of a common cause, exposure, and the effectiveness and timeliness of proposed measures, and may require a recall where necessary to address an unacceptable risk. The regulator may require an earlier recall where incident severity or other evidence shows an imminent risk. Any recall shall include direct notice to affected customers and free repair, replacement, or refund.

judge_section_notes: S1 sets strong reporting deadlines but only requires confirmed non-serious incidents to be reported. S2 keeps the 55°C test and 5% trigger but makes exceeding 5% a corrective-action matter rather than an automatic sales ban, favoring Northwind. S3 and S4 use acceptable phase-ins (6-year retrofit, 36-month suppression), while S5 weakens the 8/100k recall trigger to a corrective-action review, favoring Halcyon.
